title: How to enlarge cursor in Apple Mail on Mac: a step by step guide
metaTitle: How to enlarge cursor in Apple Mail on Mac: Easy Steps
description: Learn how to enlarge cursor on Mac to improve visibility in Apple Mail. Follow these simple system-wide accessibility steps for macOS Sequoia and earlier.
targetKeyword: how to enlarge cursor on mac
intro: To enlarge the cursor on your Mac, you must adjust your system-wide accessibility settings, as Apple Mail does not have an independent cursor control. This change will apply to Apple Mail and every other application on your computer.
tldr: Open System Settings on your Mac.
Adjust the Pointer size slider to your preferred setting.
These changes apply globally to all apps, including Apple Mail.

blocks.text: Why you cannot change the cursor inside Apple Mail

Many users look for a setting inside the Apple Mail app to change the size of their mouse pointer. It is a logical place to look when you struggle to see the cursor while drafting emails. However, Apple Mail relies on the global system settings of your Mac for its interface elements. This design choice ensures that your user experience remains consistent across all your applications. If you change your cursor size in System Settings, it updates instantly in Mail, Safari, Pages, and every other program you use.
How to enlarge cursor on Mac: Step by step
Follow these steps to increase the size of your pointer on any modern version of macOS, including Sequoia, Sonoma, and Ventura.

items: Click the Apple menu () in the top-left corner of your screen.
Select System Settings from the dropdown menu.
Click Accessibility in the left-hand sidebar.
Click Display on the right side of the window.
Move the Pointer size slider to the right to make the cursor larger.

blocks.text: Beyond just making the pointer bigger, there are other ways to make it easier to see on your screen. In the same Accessibility > Display menu, you can change the pointer outline and fill colors. A high-contrast color, such as a bright yellow or red outline, can make a huge difference if you often lose track of your mouse on a busy background.

Enable the Shake mouse pointer to locate feature. This allows you to quickly wiggle your mouse or trackpad finger to make the cursor grow temporarily. It is a great way to find your place without keeping the cursor permanently large.
blocks.title: Quickly find your cursor

blocks.text: Adjusting text size in Apple Mail

If your goal is to make reading or writing emails easier, changing the cursor size is only part of the solution. You can also change the font size within the Apple Mail app itself. Go to Mail > Settings > Fonts & Colors. Here, you can select different fonts and sizes for your messages. This does not change the font size for the recipient, only what you see on your screen.

Sometimes, the cursor size setting might not behave as expected. If you find that the changes do not take effect immediately, try restarting your Mac. If the settings are greyed out, you might be on a managed computer where your administrator has restricted access to system preferences. In that case, you will need to reach out to your IT department.

Digital accessibility is a broad topic that affects millions of people. With over 1.3 billion people living with some form of disability, tools like cursor magnification are vital for participation in the digital world. Many users rely on a combination of screen magnification, high-contrast settings, and screen readers to navigate their computers. Even if you do not have a formal vision impairment, these tools can reduce eye strain during long work sessions.

faq.question: Can I change the cursor size only for Apple Mail?
faq.answer: No. The cursor size is a system-wide setting on macOS. Changing it affects every app you use, not just Apple Mail.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to open accessibility settings?
faq.answer: Yes. You can press Command (⌘) + Option (⌥) + F5 to quickly open the Accessibility Shortcuts panel.

faq.question: Does changing the cursor size affect how others see my emails?
faq.answer: No. The cursor size is a local accessibility setting on your specific Mac. It has no impact on the emails you send or how they appear to recipients.

task: How to enlarge cursor in Apple Mail on Mac
requirements: A Mac running macOS Ventura or later

steps.name: Open System Settings
steps.text: Click the Apple menu in the top-left corner and select System Settings.

steps.name: Access Display settings
steps.text: In the sidebar, click Accessibility and then click Display.

steps.name: Adjust the pointer size
steps.text: Find the Pointer section and drag the Pointer size slider to the right to enlarge your cursor.
steps.tip: You will see the cursor grow immediately as you move the slider.

troubleshooting.problem: The cursor size did not change.
troubleshooting.fix: Ensure you are in the System Settings > Accessibility > Display menu. If it still does not work, restart your Mac.
You may be on a managed machine. Contact your IT department for permission to change these settings.
